title: Turn-aware progressive-slot batcher and slab-defrag strategy for mixed-length workloads
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (burst of short developer queries plus occasional long multi-turn assistants) cause KV cache fragmentation and GPU slab underutilization. Current continuous coalescing favors throughput but suffers P99 spikes and two classes of issues: OOMs when long-turns accumulate and wasted GPU slab slots from many short-turn KV fragments.

Goal: Implement a turn-aware progressive-slot allocation policy combined with periodic slab defragmentation and KV preemption windows to reduce tail latency and memory pressure while preserving overall throughput. The solution must be compatible with existing routing and fallback policies and togglable per-customer tier.
acceptance_criteria:
1) P99 token latency reduces by >=10% on mixed workloads (70% short / 30% long) in lab harness.
2) OOM incidents in stress tests drop to 0 for sustained 30-minute runs at 1.2x peak QPS.
3) KV hit rate for short-turn prefixes remains within 2% of baseline.
4) Feature has canary toggle and per-customer knob in console.
5) Automated regression tests for fragmentation metrics added to CI.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Initial design spike completed; measured baseline on 8xA100 harness with synthetic mix (70/30). Observed P99 = 430ms, OOMs frequent when long-turn concurrency >12.
2025-02-18: Prototype of progressive slotting implemented in batcher (experimental flag: batcher.turn_slotting_v2). Early results: P99 improved 6% but KV fragmentation metric increased.
2025-02-22: Added slab-defrag controller (heuristic: compact when fragmentation > 30% or GPU usage > 85%). Combined prototype runs show P99 improvement ~12% and OOMs eliminated in 30min stress runs.
2025-02-25: Integration with routing layer for per-customer tier toggle completed. Began writing canary rollout plan and console controls.
2025-02-28: Bench runs with real traffic replay (partner dataset) scheduled; preparing PR and confluence design doc for review.
decisions: Use turn-length histograms per slot-cohort rather than per-request prediction to avoid costly per-request ML inference in the hot path.
Progressive slot sizes: small, medium, large slots mapped to short/medium/long-turn cohorts. Slots are time-windowed and can be promoted/demoted based on recent occupancy.
KV preemption window: cold entries older than N seconds (configurable, default 45s) become eligible for preemption; preemption only runs when GPU usage > watermark to avoid regressions.
Defrag approach: in-place slab compaction during quiet GC windows; if immediate memory needed, trigger fast slab-swap fallback with minimal copy to avoid blocking inference.
Expose per-customer override in console and metric tagging for comparing behavior across Dedicated/Private clusters.
tradeoffs: Complexity: slot promotions/demotions add state in batcher and slightly more metering; improved latency justifies the added telemetry and CI coverage.
Aggressive preemption can reduce KV hit rate for long-running sessions; we mitigate via tiered windows and promotion heuristics.
Slab compaction is an expensive operation; hence we limit it to background GC windows and allow a fast-path that trades a small amount of memory for latency stability.
Per-customer knobs increase surface area for support but are necessary for enterprise customers with strict SLOs.
test_plan: Microbench: synthetic arrival streams with configurable short/long ratio, executed on 8xA100 testbed. Track P50/P95/P99, OOM count, KV hit rate, GPU memory fragmentation metric.
Replay tests: run real traffic replay from partner dataset (anonymized) at 1.2x production QPS for 30 minutes to validate stability.
Chaos tests: induce node evictions and simulate slow compaction to ensure graceful degradation and no request stalls.
Regression: add unit tests for slot promotion/demotion logic and integration tests for slab-defrag controller.
benchmarks: Baseline (70/30 synthetic) on 8xA100: P99 = 430ms, OOMs observed when long-turn concurrency >12, KV fragmentation = 38%.
Turn-aware + slab-defrag prototype: P99 = 378ms (12% improvement), zero OOMs in 30min stress runs, KV fragmentation reduced to 18%, overall token cost ~7% lower.
Edge-case: 95/5 short/long mix saw negligible throughput impact and maintained low fragmentation after slot promotion tuning.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag default off. 2) Canary: enable for 5% of hosted traffic on non-critical region for 48 hours with automated rollback on P99 regression >5% or OOMs. 3) Ramp to 25% then 60% over 4 days while monitoring fragmentation and token cost. 4) Enable for Dedicated clusters only after customer opt-in and run additional stress test. 5) Document console knobs and add runbook for slab-defrag incidents.
notes: Follow-up: evaluate adding a lightweight per-request predictor for cases where slot histograms diverge rapidly (edge customers with bursty long-turns).
Ops: add alert for repeated defrag cycles within 10 minutes (possible workload pattern change or leak).
UX: PM to add a short blurb in Console explaining when to enable preemption for Dedicated customers.
